profiles: Every release and native setting pinned in server-projection-v1.json.
scope: One single-target UPDATE. The ordered assignments write declared writable signed integer columns. Each right operand is a signed integer literal, explicit NULL or a signed integer column from the same row. WHERE uses the registered native predicate roles.
open: Other scalar roles, UPDATE FROM and joined targets, assignment rows, WITH, conflict modifiers, RETURNING, ORDER BY and row bounds
Generated and identity targets and writes requesting DEFAULT

invariants: A nonempty owned list of at most 1024 ordered assignments
Each written and read slot belongs to the target layout
Every scope in this statement has only one input occurrence
Update.meaning: Select matching rows using the pre-assignment predicate. MySQL assignments read the current row in written order. PostgreSQL assignments read the old row. Update the same external objects, including PostgreSQL descendant tables unless ONLY applies.
Update.sql: Emit the absolute target and its canonical alias, followed by the checked assignments in order and the optional filter. PostgreSQL emits ONLY for the named-only scan.

UpdateAssignment.role: One ordered write to a slot of the target row
invariants: The target is a zero-occurrence column reference
Right operands use the signed literal, NULL or row reference roles
The UPDATE boundary checks actual membership of both read and write references

analysis: Read the declared relation identity and inheritance policy from binding. Resolve each named write column to a writable signed 32-bit declaration. Allocate the read and write slots in the same target. Close the ordered assignments and the optional predicate using the public constructors.
observations: Native affected-row count from the fixed client profile
Complete before and after target, independent control and PostgreSQL child contents
Typed before and after row-trigger records

finite.completeness: Verify the exact product of independently fixed layouts, assignment forms, filter forms and policies in the observed runtime values.

negative: A read reference outside the target
A write reference outside the target
A WHERE reference outside the target
faults: Write to the wrong target slot
evidence: Preserve actual typed state and emitted SQL on exact runtime bytes. Compare an independent old-row or current-row interpreter with the native engine and check that the fixture is restored.
trust: Closed runtime rules and declared relation facts
Deterministic fixture table definitions and observers
Native expression profile and effect model
